en: The *Dhāraṇī of the Dharma-Treasury of Mañjuśrī*, spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling in the palace of the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven together with the great bodhisattvas...
The assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
as well as immeasurable sons of the gods from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens,
surrounded the Tathāgata on all sides, making offerings, paying homage, showing respect, praising him, and gazing up at him with veneration.
At that time, the World-Honored One was amidst the assembly,
expounding immeasurable and wondrous dharmas of dharanis for the great multitude.
Furthermore, it was for the sake of benefiting those sentient beings of meager merit in future ages.
He then entered a samādhi called "Radiating Light.
From the crown of his head, he emitted immeasurable varieties of light;
these rays circled back and forth, illuminating immeasurable and boundless Buddha-worlds.
Having shone [upon them], the light returned and circled around the youth Mañjuśrī,
then entered the crown of his head.
Once the light had entered through the crown, it...
Mañjuśrī immediately entered a samādhi called the Sovereign King of Dhāraṇīs.
Having entered this samādhi...
Immediately, from his mouth, he emitted immeasurable rays of light of various colors and forms.
Once these rays had issued forth,
they entered into the crown of the head of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secret Traces,
rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and joined his palms toward the Buddha.
With deep reverence, he prostrated himself and gazed upon the Blessed One’s countenance, addressing him thus: "World-Honored One, in the past you spoke these words to me:
'After my Dharma has perished, during the evil age in Jambudvīpa...'"
Mañjuśrī is extensively able to benefit immeasurable sentient beings and shall perform the work of a Buddha.
I pray that the World-Honored One will analyze and explain for me:
in what place does he dwell, and in which direction does he act to bring about such benefit?
"Out of compassion and for the sake of protecting all sentient beings,
I pray that you will explain it.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Mysteries, saying:
"Noble son, it is well that you have been able to pose this question to me for the sake of all sentient beings.
Excellent, excellent! Listen attentively now, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well.
I shall now explain it to you in detail."
At that time, having heard the Buddha’s words, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secret Traces, was filled with joy and leaped for gladness;
he adjusted his robes and listened with single-minded attention.
Then the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secret Traces, saying:
After my parinirvāṇa, in this Jambudvīpa, in the northeast,
there will be a country named Mahācīna.
Within that country, there is a mountain called Pañcaśīrṣa.
The youth Mañjuśrī wandered and resided there,
preaching the Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings;
there were also immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others.
They surrounded him, making offerings and paying him homage.
Thereupon, the Blessed One again addressed the Lord Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"This is the youth Mañjuśrī."
Possessing such immeasurable majesty and virtue,
with the sovereign adornment of supernatural powers and transformations,
he is extensively able to benefit all sentient beings.
The power of his perfected and complete merit is inconceivable.
He then addressed Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Mysteries, saying:
"Mañjuśrī possesses a dhāraṇī, a most supreme and profoundly secret heart-mantra."
Together with the methods for painting images and the maṇḍala mudrās:
in the future final age, when the Buddha-dharma is extinguished and evil dharmas increase,
and when various calamities arise— at such a time as this.
In the future world, among the beings of Jambudvīpa who possess meager merit and little wisdom, evil karma will increase;
the five elements will lose their order and the yin and yang will become disordered.
Wind and rain will become unseasonable, and malevolent stars will manifest strange portents.
Strife and battle between devas and asuras will break out;
the devas will diminish while the asuras increase.
At such a time, various calamities will circulate throughout the world;
malevolent spirits will descend and transform themselves into female forms.
They inflict various diseases upon sentient beings,
namely: throat obstructions, carbuncles, scabies, leprosy, abdominal pains,
and malarial fevers that recur every one, two, three, or four days.
This continues until it erupts once every seven days;
or one may suffer from diseases of wind, bile, or phlegm, or all three combined,
including headaches, boils, swellings, and eye pain.
Regarding various ailments such as dysentery involving stool and urine,
malevolent ghosts and spirits may transform their bodies into those of insects, wolves, tigers, leopards, lions, and all manner of other beasts.
Within this world, they gather in all sentient beings;
they consume their vital essence, causing their majesty to vanish and their strength to decline. At such a time, within Jambudvīpa—
Innumerable sentient beings meet with untimely and unjust deaths;
even though there may be physicians, they are unable to provide a cure.
During such an era, in a single day, there are thirty *vimatra* counts.
Therefore, Vajra, I now entrust this to you to bestow upon sentient beings.
I shall teach this dharani method so that it may be received and maintained through successive transmission.
Why is this? Because of all the sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa.
Constantly give rise to the great and virtuous aspiration for bodhicitta:
"When shall we be able to escape this ocean of afflictions and the prison of ignorance and craving?
For this reason, I cause you to constantly teach and widely disseminate [this teaching].
May they develop right faith toward the Buddha’s stūpas and the Triple Gem;
may they cultivate wholesome deeds and refrain from unrighteousness;
and may they be filial toward their parents and respectful toward their teachers and elders.
Toward all those who are virtuous and noble, they conceive a sense of wonder;
they constantly provide offerings of flowers, incense, the hundred flavors of sweet delicacies,
and honor, revere, respect, and praise them.
Recite this most supreme dhāraṇī for seven days and seven nights, observing the eightfold precepts (aṣṭāṅga-upavāsa) every day.
You must also recite these various dhāraṇīs.
At that time, the Tathāgata, out of great compassion and pity,
immediately spoke this *dhāraṇī* of the Tathāgata Vistīrṇagambhīrajñānagarjiteśvararāja, saying:

*Namo vimalabuddhyanirjātarājāya tathāgatāya | tadyathā | vimalanirdeśe vimalasvare vimalayoniśe anāsrave anāsrasaṃgate saṃgate svāhā.* Next, he spoke the *dhāraṇī* of the Tathāgata Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin.
Namo sarvanirvaraṇaviṣkambhitathāgatāya | tadyathā | he maṃ he maṃ he maṃ he maṃ svāhā || Next, the dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata Amitābha is taught:
*Namo mitābhāya tathāgatāya | tadyathā | amṛtodbhave | amṛte | amṛtavikrāntite svāhā* || Next, the Tathāgata-dhāraṇī of the Place of Merit is taught.
Namo yuṣaṇākarāya tathāgatāya | tadyathā | gaganale gaganasvapaye gaganagatike svāhā || Next, the dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata Samantāvabhāsagandha is taught:
Namo samantabhadraya tathāgatāya | tadyathā | oṃ samaye svāhā || Next, the dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata Durdharṣacaryā is taught.
Namo 'parimitāyur-jñāna-sūtra-garbhe tathāgatāya tadyathā | mā-maṃ svāhā. Next, the Tathāgata’s dhāraṇī for removing pride is taught.
*Namo maṇasvambhāya tathāgatāya | tadyathā | manubhiśuṇḍe manubhiruṇḍane svāhā.* Next, the Tathāgata’s dhāraṇī for severing all obstacles is taught:
Namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ | Namo sarvavidrāṇaviśuddhiviniṣṭhitatathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya ||

Tadyathā: śvete karebi jvalitiye svāhā | jambhani stambhani mohani svāhā | bhaṇḍalikāya svāhā | hūṃ dharma-dharma-jñaptaye svāhā | dare vidare karaviṅka-rudraye svāhā | śānte kṣānti-jvalapane svāhā | dhuru dhuru vidhuru jaye svāhā | padma-savale padma-sambhave cikale hitaṅkariye svāhā. Next, the Dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Candraprabha is taught:
Namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ | tadyathā | candraprabhe | candranakhavicitrasvati | sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhitānugrhīte svāhā || Next, the mantra of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva is taught:
Namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya tadyathā | jāte jāte jaye jyāye jvale vajre mahāmāṃsāya svāhā || Next, the dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara is taught.
Namo 'riya-vairocani-śvarāya bodhisattvāya tadyathā | gaganadhṛk gaganasamudgate gagana-vikrānti e-maṃ mañju-maṃjari svāhā || Next, the dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra is spoken.
Namo ārya-kumārabhūtāya bodhisattvāya. Tadyathā: he vajre mahāvajre ativajre vigatarāgasi mahāvigatarāgasi he mivati karmavāraṇe viśuddhe svāhā. Next, the dhāraṇī of Maitreya Bodhisattva is taught.
*Namo ’rthyamaitriyāya bodhisattvāya tadyathā maitri maitri maitramanasi svāhā.* Next, the dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha is taught.
Namo āryakṣāntimati-satvāya | tadyathā | akṣaye | prākṣaye | prākṣayakarma-viśodhani | svāhā || Next, the dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati is spoken.
*Namo ’rya-akṣaya-mati-satvāya tadyathā | akṣaye akṣaye akṣaye akṣaye akṣaya-karma-viśodhani svāhā* || Next, the dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Vimalakīrti is spoken:

Namo 'rthyavimalakīrtaye bhūtasa-tvāya | tadyathā | jyotiḥ sarvaniratijite | sarvārthavajrakare | vajrabhāve | vajravainākare | svāhā | Next, the dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin is taught.
Namo sarvavidyāraṇābhiṣekāṇi jinaputrāya tadyathā | sarvavidyāraṇābhiṣeka svāhā dhātu-vigata svāhā ||
Namaḥ kamalāyai svāhā | Namaḥ avajitakāye svāhā | Namaḥ malanandane svāhā | Namaḥ bodhigarbhanandane svāhā | Namaḥ karmānirvartikāyai svāhā ||
Oṃ vīrye svāhā | Oṃ kāramaye svāhā | Oṃ yugañjaye svāhā | Oṃ sarvabuddhaviśuddhaye svāhā | Oṃ mṛgaṅkabāṇadhare svāhā ||
Namaḥ sarvadharmāniścitāye svāhā. Namaḥ sarvabuddhaniṣṭhitāye svāhā.
Namaḥ khaṅgaviṣāṇāye svāhā. Namaḥ aśvalāṅgāye svāhā. Namaḥ abhyudgatāye svāhā.
Oṃ hā āmbudaye svāhā | Sarvānukūlabhadre svāhā | Next, the Moonlight Youth Dhāraṇī is taught.
*Namo jñānaprabhāvaguptāya tadyathā | pravīḥ prabhāvati dharmaviśuddhidevatāyai svāhā.* At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, saying:
If there are sons or daughters of good family who recite this eighteen-deity dhāraṇī for seven days and seven nights,
all their past and present offenses of the three karmas shall be [purified].
All obstacles whatsoever shall be completely extinguished, and body and mind shall be purified.
All worldly ailments of wind and bile,
as well as all other diseases and afflictions, shall be entirely cured and eliminated.
All the ghosts and spirits— the pūtana demons, the mad-making demons, yakṣas, rākṣasas, graha-seizing spirits, piśāca spirits, and nākinī spirits,
as well as those who suck the vital essence from humans— [were subdued].
All other ghosts and spirits will always remain twelve yojanas away from this person,
as well as famine, pestilence, and other diseases.
They shall not be harmed by calamities such as wind, thunder, lightning,
or thunderbolts. If men or women suffer from misfortune or disaster,
they should install a stūpa containing śarīra relics along with an image of the Buddha within their residence.
Paint an image of the youth Mañjuśrī.
Burn various incenses, such as aloeswood, frankincense, and the like;
light lamps and scatter flowers, along with exquisite fruits, melons, and a variety of choice delicacies.
Every day, they shall provide food for seven bhikṣus,
copy, uphold, read, and recite this sutra, practice according to the Dharma,
and with a diligent mind, chant and circumambulate the stupa while walking the path.
All afflictions and other calamities shall be entirely extinguished.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Within this Dharma-treasury of Mañjuśrī, there is a true Dharma, a most supreme Dharma, a peerless Dharma."
They can act as a wish-fulfilling jewel for sentient beings and cause the ten wholesome deeds to be diligently promoted in whatever land they reside.
If a king practices the ten wholesome deeds, [the same shall apply].
"Whatever the king undertakes shall all be brought to fulfillment.
These eight characters of the Great Majestic Power Dhāraṇī were spoken in the past by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
For the sake of protecting all kings who practice the ten virtuous actions,
may they obtain their heart's desire, long life,
and incomparable, preeminent fruits of merit.
The military forces of all directions shall completely cease, and the realm shall be peaceful and secure.
All that belongs to the king shall constantly increase,
for this dhāraṇī benefits and has compassion for all sentient beings.
It can sever the three evil realms and bring about all dharmas of peace and security,
no different from the Buddha currently dwelling in the world.
This is the body of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
For the sake of benefiting sentient beings,
he manifests this body in the form of a mantra-deity,
capable of fulfilling all aspirations and other such matters.
If a person can hear and recollect this dhāraṇī even for a brief moment,
they will be able to extinguish such offenses as the four pārājika transgressions and the five ānantarya crimes;
how much more so if they constantly recite it!
At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken these words,
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, regarding the eight-character Mahātejas-dhāraṇī that the Tathāgata previously expounded,"
"What are they? I only pray that you will explain them.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secret Traces, saying:
Listen attentively, listen attentively! I shall now explain it for you.
These eight characters are known as the Great Majestic Virtue Secret Heart Dhāraṇī;
they are no different from the Buddha remaining in the world.
It is able to act as a great bright lamp for all sentient beings within the darkness.
At that time, the Tathāgata spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:
*Namo aparimitāyur-jñāna-viniścaya-rāja-dhāriṇe tathāgatāya | Namo mañjuśrī-kumārabhūtāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ āḥ vīra hūṃ khaḥ jaḥ svāhā.* Then the Blessed One addressed Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Mysteries.
Regarding these eight syllables called the "Supremely Victorious Great Majestic Power Heart Mantra":
wherever they abide, it is no different from the Buddha being present in person;
they can manifest the various inconceivable supernatural powers of all Buddhas.
It is also capable of performing great supernatural transformations and manifestations.
I shall now briefly praise a small portion of this dhāraṇī’s efficacy;
were I to explain it in full, [it would be endless].
It could not be fully expounded even in immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of great kalpas.
O Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets,
if there are men or women who are unable to perform the rites of service and offering for this dhāraṇī, [they should...]
Householders are pressed by the various duties of the household;
they can only maintain [the teachings] in memory without forgetting them and recite them at the proper times.
Providing offerings according to one's means, even if they are few,
will also lead to accomplishment,
provided that one is not lacking in sincerity or right faith.
They do not give rise to the Mahāyāna bodhicitta;
they engage in slander toward the Triple Gem and give rise to unwholesome states of mind,
performing various evil deeds.
For such persons, even all minor dharmas will not be accomplished,
let alone the great dharma. At that time,
the Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Mysteries, saying:
If there are good men or good women who can recite this dhāraṇī even once, they will be able to protect themselves;
with two recitations, they can protect their companions.
Reciting it three times provides great protection;
even Bodhisattvas dwelling on the ten stages cannot surpass it,
let alone lesser beings.
If one recites it four times, one will obtain protection for all members of one's household, great and small.
Five times, one can protect all one's kinsmen and dependents.
Six times, one can protect all cities, towns, villages, and the like.
Reciting it seven times will enable one to protect all sentient beings.
When about to put on clothes, one should empower them by reciting it seven times;
this can eliminate all evil poisons and various calamities.
When washing one's hands or face, one should empower the water by reciting [the mantra] seven times;
this will cause all beings to give rise to feelings of noble esteem,
and all malevolent spirits and ghosts who see it shall be completely subdued.
All people will again come to revere them;
their evil minds will be subdued and they will give rise to hearts of joy.
If a person suffers from pain in the body or its limbs and joints, [they shall be relieved].
If one consecrates warm water one hundred and eight times and bathes with it,
one will immediately be cured. Furthermore,
if one rises early each day and drinks a handful of water that has been consecrated seven times, [the same result will follow].
All karmic retributions pertaining to the body will be completely extinguished, let alone those who are free from calamities;
furthermore, their three types of karma will be cleansed away,
and they shall attain a long life.
If one consecrates food and drink seven times and consumes it,
no poisons whatsoever shall be able to cause harm. Furthermore,
if one encounters wicked people or sees enemies, [they shall likewise be unable to cause harm].
One should recite this mantra.
All enemies who give rise to evil intentions shall naturally be subdued;
they will eliminate their anger and turn toward one with a heart of loving-kindness.
In places where there is fear, one should recite this mantra with a sincere mind, and immediately the fear will be dispelled.
If one wishes to lie down to sleep, one should recite this mantra one hundred and eight times;
then one will have auspicious dreams and come to know matters of both good and evil.
If there is someone suffering from various types of malarial fevers,
the practitioner should gaze at the face of the afflicted person and recite the eight-syllable mantra one thousand and eight times with earnest application; they will then be cured.
When intending to enter a battle array,
one should write this mantra upon paper using ox-gall (gorocanā) and wear it upon the body.
No swords, staves, bows, arrows, spears, or axes shall be able to cause harm.
When entering an army formation, one should draw an image of the youth Mañjuśrī along with his mantra and place it upon an elephant or horse.
When led at the head of an army,
various military forces and bandits will be unable to cause harm and will naturally retreat and disperse.
The painted image should be depicted with the appearance of a youth.
Riding upon a golden peacock,
all bandits who see him will retreat and scatter. If one constantly recites [this mantra], [the same result shall follow].
All offenses, including the five heinous crimes and the four grave transgressions, shall be completely extinguished.
One will constantly behold Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva face-to-face.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, one must always recite and maintain this in mind without forgetting.
Recite one hundred and eight times each time without interruption;
you will always cause all sentient beings to submit and take refuge.
If you empower your topknot seven times, [the same result shall follow].
All sentient beings who see it will be completely subdued, and evil people will retreat and disperse.
If one can recite this one hundred and eight times during each of the three periods of the day, [the benefits shall be attained].
All actions will accord with one’s intentions, and all sought-after aspirations will be fulfilled according to one’s heart's desire.
Everything shall be attained in complete perfection and abundance;
one will achieve great wealth and nobility, and one’s conduct will be sovereign and unimpeded.
At the time of their death, they shall attain the Samantamukha-samādhi and personally behold Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secret Traces, saying:
Good son, as for this Mañjuśrī dhāraṇī, if there are kings,
princes, queens, princesses, or various high-ranking officials who are able to transcribe it and place it within their residences;
One shall attain great wealth and honor, and all calamities shall be entirely extinguished.
All sought-after aspirations shall be fully realized,
and one shall constantly be surrounded and protected by benevolent deities.
It shall not allow ghosts or demons to come and harass or afflict them.
At that time, the Buddha again addressed the Lord of Guhyakas, saying:
"This secret dhāraṇī is inconceivable."
The majestic power of all Buddhas is likewise inconceivable.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni again addressed the Lord Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"This eight-syllable secret majestic great dhāraṇī..."
Furthermore, there is the method of painting images which benefits all beings;
this was taught by those who practice the ten wholesome paths as kings.
If there are good sons or good daughters, [who...]
By maintaining this dhāraṇī, one will obtain great protection with little effort;
furthermore, it can protect all princes, queens, palace attendants, maidservants, and the various ministers and high officials.
As well as the men and women, including the scholars of the land—
all the people and their fields and houses—
every such thing shall be entirely peaceful and happy.
If anyone can install these painted images wherever they may be,
then kings, thieves, water, fire, weapons, bandits,
and all such calamities will be entirely pacified and extinguished.
Furthermore, untimely epidemics, droughts, and floods shall all be eliminated;
damage from insects and frost shall likewise be extinguished.
May the Dragon Kings always cause rain to fall in its proper season, so that the crops may ripen in abundance.
The people of the land were peaceful and joyful, free from all calamities and disasters.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secret Traces, addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
"Regarding the methods for the vast painted images and so forth that were previously mentioned, how should they be made? We pray that you will explain them.
At that time, the World-Honored One replied:
Good son, whenever one wishes to paint an image,
one must first seek out a superior, fine, and white cotton cloth. Next,
one must select an auspicious day and lunar mansion, with favorable planetary alignments, such as the conjunction of Venus (太白).
It is auspicious to perform this during the favorable hours of the day;
thereafter, one should paint the image.
In a clean place, one should sprinkle and sweep it with scented water.
One should take kumuda mud to smear upon the ground,
hang various banners and canopies, burn aloeswood and other incenses, and offer precious delicacies as an offering.
The cloth must be eight cubits wide and twelve cubits long.
First, in the center, paint Śākyamuni Buddha,
seated upon a lotus throne made of the seven precious gems in the posture of preaching the Dharma.
To the right of the Buddha, paint Mañjuśrī.
He has the appearance of a youth, wearing a jeweled crown upon his head and various ornaments such as necklaces around his neck;
his body is the color of *uragasāra* gold, and with a joyful countenance, he gazes up at the Tathāgata.
Next, on the right side, paint the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Next, paint the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
Next, on the left side of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, one should paint the Bodhisattva Maitreya, [accompanied by] the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati.
Next, paint the Bodhisattva Vimalakīrti;
next, paint the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin;
next, paint the youth Candraprabha.
Next, paint the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha.
All the aforementioned bodhisattvas and others are each seated upon pedestals of seven-jeweled lotus flowers.
In all cases, one must depict the actual form,
down to the objects held in the hands;
all should be drawn according to the original ritual manual.
Do not allow anything to be omitted or lost.
Furthermore, above Śākyamuni Tathāgata,
paint the seven buddhas.
Namely, the Tathāgata Vast Wisdom Profound Thunder-Sound King,
the Tathāgata Remover of All Obstructions,
and the Tathāgata Amitābha.
The Tathāgata Guṇasthāna,
the Tathāgata Samantagandha,
and the Tathāgata Durjayavīravanirghoṣacaryā.
The Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
These seven Buddhas must all be painted in sequence;
their bodies are all golden in color, each in the posture of preaching the Dharma.
At the two upper corners of the painted image,
there shall be depicted two celestial beings (devaputra),
each wearing a floral garland upon their heads; one hand holds a flower, while the other hand scatters flowers.
With half his body hidden within the clouds,
his form was upright and handsome, and he adorned his body with necklaces made of various kinds of the seven treasures.
Beneath the lotus flower of that Śākyamuni Buddha, [he sat].
Paint two dragon kings:
the first named Nanda and the second named Upananda.
Both of these dragon kings emerge from the Anavatapta Lake with their upper bodies half-visible.
With their hands, they supported and together grasped the lotus stalk upon which Śākyamuni Tathāgata sat,
applying a forceful and respectful effort;
both of these dragon kings assumed human faces.
Upon each head, seven snake heads are depicted;
their heads are all white and their bodies take human form,
adorned with various miscellaneous jewels.
All gaze upward with their eyes beholding the Tathāgata. Below Mañjuśrī,
